art.subject: Roseate Tern (Sterna dougallii), adult in breeding plumage, as a summer vagrant: glossy black cap from the bill base to the nape; upperparts and wings very pale silvery grey, paler than in other Sterna terns, the outermost two or three primaries darker grey and forming a narrow dark edge to the folded wingtip; rump and tail white, the outer tail feathers forming very long white streamers; underparts white with a delicate pink flush on the breast and belly. Bill long and slender, mostly red in summer, with black mainly along the upper mandible and at the tip (blackish only early in the season); dark eye; legs bright orange-red.
art.pose: standing on a rock with the long tail streamers clear of the wingtips, side view
art.scene: Rocky offshore islet off Korea's south coast in mid-summer, bright sun over a blue sea; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding, side view standing on a rock: black cap reaching far down the nape, slender bill red with black mainly on the upper mandible, very pale grey back and wings with darker outermost primaries along the folded wingtip, white underparts with a rosy flush, very long white tail streamers, short orange-red legs

adult breeding, in flight seen squarely from above: head, body and tail in one line, inner wings straight out to the sides and outer wings angled back at the wrist, very pale grey upperwings and mantle with darker outermost primaries, black cap, very long deeply forked white tail
art.build: Slender, medium-small tern, smaller and slimmer than Black-headed Gull. Bill slender, about as long as the head, straight and fine-tipped. Legs short, red. Wings relatively short for a tern; at rest the tail streamers project well beyond the wingtips. In flight the upperwing looks almost white except for the darker outermost primaries, and the underwing is white with no dark trailing edge to the primaries; wingbeats rapid, stiff and shallow; plunge-dives for fish.
avoid: Do not paint grey underparts or a dark trailing edge under the primaries (Common Tern); the Roseate is white below with a pink tinge.
Do not make the tail streamers short or hidden by the wings; they extend well beyond the wingtips.
Do not paint a white crown with only a black band on the nape (Black-naped Tern, Sterna sumatrana).
Do not darken the upperparts; they are the palest of all Sterna terns.
Do not paint an all-black bill with only a trace of red at the base (European birds); East Asian Roseate Terns become largely red-billed in summer.
